correctness.rationale: The precise immediate-child, unlabelled, finite tree semantics yield exactly 16 depth-three types. The local distinct-child weighted demand inequality sums over each nonroot vertex exactly once, giving n >= sum_v h(t(v)) + lambda_beta(root). The 16 potentials are nonnegative and total 44. Root type >=4 forces root weight >=3, so n>=47 for every tree. A standalone checker verifies a 47-vertex rooted arborescence, its 16 calculated types and the equality certificate.

value.rationale: The result answers a natural complete finite saturation problem: the least rooted immediate-child tree representing all modal depth-three observational classes. It measures the cost of forbidding shared descendants, compared with the 16-vertex DAG construction; its exact 47 barrier is supported by an explicit structural potential lower bound, not an arbitrary computation. There is no claimed or needed general theorem for other modal depths.
